title: The hypertrophy series: deloading without wasting tonnage
summary: NH argues that deloads are a strength/powerlifting practice that bodybuilders should not copy: needing one means the program overreaches. Instead he recommends keeping tonnage stable via exercise rotations and sustainable intensity windows of roughly 70-90%.
claims: Deloads are first and foremost a strength practice and are counterproductive for bodybuilders
Taking a week off to deload is catastrophic; time off should only happen with injury or when away from the gym
Even massively reducing load for 3-4 days is too much and shows you either misunderstand size training or you are exceeding your maximum recoverable volume
Powerlifters deload because strength must peak at a specific time; bodybuilding never needs a peak
Powerlifting maximises strength while bodybuilding stabilises strength to provide a steady intake of tonnage
Tonnage should never experience massive dips or massive increases; it should stay stable and slowly creep up
The real benefits of a deload are physical recovery and mental respite, and both can be obtained through programming
Exercise rotations give mental respite by keeping the program fresh and reduce overuse injuries by changing the movement pattern
Swap heavy back squats every other session for a variation such as front squat, belt squat or good morning to keep stress and tonnage while getting distance from the lift
Needing a deload means you are digging a hole: training too frequently, too much volume, or too much strength work
Strength work is important for bodybuilding but should be a minority of the tonnage
It is better to cut 40-50 minutes from your week's training than to be forced to deload
Tonnage lost during a deload exceeds what you lose by voluntarily trimming the program; a self-imposed limitation beats a forced one
Powerlifters deload after peaking or peak intensity, which bodybuilders don't need
He always trains between 70 and 90-95% intensity, around 90% for most lifts, and never higher
You don't need super high intensity to grow, just intensity; steady 85-95% beats swinging between 99% and 60%
If deloads help you progress keep them; if they put you in a rut, try his stable-tonnage method
